clue.text: Child listens, confused about Christopher Biggins's last film

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters wrap round the first and last letters taken next
confused says the letters of these two words are muddled into a new order
last picks the final letter of each of the two names it follows

explanation.surface: A child hears the entertainer Christopher Biggins's latest film described and gets muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' jumbles the first two words, and 'about' wraps them round the final letters of the two names. Christopher Biggins is a British TV and pantomime personality.
explanation.definitionFit: Spielberg's 1993 Holocaust drama is an example of a film.

clue.text: Nasty stuff in science fiction parody

indicators.note: in says the nasty stuff goes inside the genre abbreviation

parts.note: poo is excrement, nasty stuff

explanation.surface: Nasty material in a sci-fi story turns out to be a send-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A humorous imitation that mocks its original is a send-up or lampoon.

clue.text: It's produced internally when groom collapses

indicators.note: collapses says the letters of these two words fall apart and are reassembled

explanation.surface: Something emerges from within at a wedding when the groom faints.
explanation.definitionFit: Produce grown in one's own garden or country is made locally, not imported.

clue.text: We leave Cornish resort upside- down to get old fabric

indicators.note: to get says the remaining letters take in the letter for old
leave says those two letters depart from what remains
upside-down in a down answer means the resort's name is read bottom to top

parts.note: Newlyn is a fishing town and resort in Cornwall

explanation.surface: We quit a Cornish seaside town, turned upside down, to find an old cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: Reversing first is what lets 'leave' find the pair in order. Newlyn is a fishing town in Cornwall, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The synthetic polymer used for stockings and clothing is a fabric.

clue.text: Disoriented, our side hides at the bottom

indicators.note: hides says the word for disoriented conceals the pronoun inside it

parts.note: to be disoriented is to be lost
we are our side, as opposed to them

explanation.surface: Bewildered, our team skulks at the foot of the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Being deepest or least high, last in a ranking, is being at the very bottom.

clue.text: Cancel beer in King George having turned up at ease

indicators.note: turned up in a down answer means the whole assembly is read bottom to top
in says the two words go inside the royal cipher

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George
to nix is to cancel
ale is beer

explanation.surface: A king called George cancels beer, then shows up looking calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having turned up' reverses the whole assembly, not just the royal cipher, as this is a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwinding and resting is being at ease, the participle describing someone untroubled.

clue.text: Shirker with bye in zonals getting shafted

indicators.note: getting shafted means badly treated, so the letters of the two words are mangled

explanation.surface: A layabout team given a bye in the zonal round gets cheated.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazy person who avoids work is a shirker, idler or slacker.

clue.text: Hospital volunteers seen in many places in Mexico

definitions.text: seen in many places in Mexico

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital
the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Hospital volunteers turn up across Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish for saint begins many Mexican place names, such as Santa Ana and Santa Rosalía.

clue.text: Politicians remaining on street in Iceland

parts.note: left means remaining, as in 'what is left'

indicators.note: in says the street abbreviation sits inside the country code

parts.note: IS is the international code for Iceland

explanation.surface: Politicians are still out on the street in Iceland.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters of the left are politically active people, here taken as politicians.

clue.text: I'm surprised by medium salad being something important for electricians

parts.note: the exclamation oh expresses surprise
M is the standard abbreviation for medium, as on clothing sizes
slaw, short for coleslaw, is a cabbage salad

explanation.surface: Someone gasps at a mid-sized salad that turns out to matter to electricians.
explanation.definitionFit: The rule relating voltage, current and resistance is fundamental knowledge in electrical work.

clue.text: Diamond system for living in a box

indicators.note: in says the philosophy sits inside the theatre box

parts.note: a loge is a box in a theatre
Zen is a Buddhist approach to life

explanation.surface: A diamond-shaped scheme for life squeezed into a box, like a lifestyle sold in a package.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus shape, as on a road sign or in heraldry, is called by this name as well as diamond.

clue.text: Dickensian description of smoker's mouth

definitions.meaning: the old thief who runs the boys' gang in Oliver Twist is a character from Dickens
a smoker's mouth has a cigarette (British slang

explanation.surface: A Victorian-style word-picture of a smoker's mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words the answer is FAG IN: FAG is everyday British slang for a cigarette, so it describes a mouth holding one.
explanation.definitionFit: The criminal mentor of Oliver Twist is one of Dickens's best-known characters.

clue.text: Film live when following male, typically in a group

indicators.note: in says the chromosome pair and the next two words sit inside the group

parts.note: a set is a group of things

indicators.note: following says the verb and conjunction come after the chromosomes

parts.note: a male typically has XY sex chromosomes
to be is to live or exist
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A film about living with a man, most likely as part of a gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' splits the group word after its second letter. Sexy Beast is a 2000 British gangster film.
explanation.definitionFit: The 2000 British gangster film starring Ray Winstone and Ben Kingsley has this title.

clue.text: Leaving old cheat to back American

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: to back here means the word for cheat runs backwards

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them
US stands for American, as in US troops

explanation.surface: An old swindler is leaving to support an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like 'support', but 'to back' reverses the cheat word.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass departure, like that of the Israelites from Egypt, is a leaving.

clue.text: Shows former Scottish football team retains charisma

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: retains says the team name holds the charisma word inside it

parts.note: Hibs is the nickname of Hibernian, an Edinburgh football club
it can mean sex appeal or charisma, as in the 'It girl'

explanation.surface: Displays show that a former Scottish club still has its star quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Items put on display in a museum are exhibits; as a verb it is a synonym for shows.

clue.text: Arm shockingly purple, setter's breakdown starts

indicators.note: shockingly says the letters of the colour are jolted out of order

parts.note: setter's means the setter is, I'm, from the compiler's viewpoint

indicators.note: starts takes the opening letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: An arm that has turned a shocking purple, and the setter is beginning to fall apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The arm is anatomically the upper extremity of the body, as opposed to the leg.

clue.text: University's new kids nursery initially has people with no reputation

indicators.note: initially says take the opening letter of each of the four words before it

parts.note: to own is to have

explanation.surface: A university's new nursery for children takes in people nobody has heard of.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures no one has heard of, such as untried actors, are nobodies without fame.

clue.text: Heated about clearing out the harmful grain processor

indicators.note: about says the word for heated goes round the letters that are left

parts.note: heated means warm

indicators.note: clearing out removes the middle of the little word, leaving its two ends

parts.note: ill can mean harmful, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: An angry protest about getting rid of something harmful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clearing out' empties the little word of its middle letter, keeping only its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill turned by a water wheel grinds corn into flour, processing grain.

clue.text: Which cemetery has pride?

parts.note: a cemetery has ... it, while pride is one of the seven deadly sins, a serious wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A riddle asking which burial ground boasts pride.
explanation.walkthrough: Split one way the answer is GRAVES IN, what every cemetery has; split as written it is a serious sin, which pride is.
explanation.definitionFit: Pride heads the seven deadly sins, so it is a serious moral offence.

clue.text: Back down on standard content for sign

indicators.note: content for says the next pieces are the stuffing put inside the word for sign

parts.note: a hint is a sign or clue
D is an abbreviation for down, as in crossword clue numbers
par is the standard, as in 'up to par'

explanation.surface: A note about a standard being lowered, in the language of a signboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content for' means the two pieces are the filling of the sign word.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear section of an animal or object is its rear, the back.

clue.text: Things being so advanced, rest on current square

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
to sit is to rest
I is the symbol for electric current
S can stand for square, as in sq or s in measurements

explanation.surface: With things moving forward, someone rests on the current town square.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in the present state of affairs, describing how matters stand.

clue.text: Political figure's grand article on democratic Pacific state

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand
an is the indefinite article
D stands for Democrat or democratic, as in US politics
HI is the postal abbreviation for Hawaii, the US state in the Pacific

explanation.surface: A politician's impressive essay about a democratic island state in the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: The leader of Indian independence is one of history's best-known political figures.

clue.text: Call Saucer, as might be said in up-market area

indicators.note: as might be said says the answer is how the two words would sound spoken

parts.note: a call on the phone is a ring, a bell; one who adds more gravy is jokingly a gravier, a saucer

explanation.surface: An instruction to phone someone who pours sauce, said in a posh accent.
explanation.walkthrough: BELL (call) and GRAVIER (one who serves gravy, a saucer) spoken with a non-rhotic British accent give the answer. Belgravia is an expensive district of central London.
explanation.definitionFit: The London district near Belgrave Square is famous for grand houses and wealthy residents.

clue.text: Partially reveal a thick stick

indicators.note: Partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Show a bit of a thick stick.
explanation.definitionFit: In India a heavy bamboo staff carried by police is a type of cudgel.

clue.text: Cancel loan, having received credit

indicators.note: having received says the loan takes the credit letters inside it

parts.note: a sub is an advance or loan on wages
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: Write off a loan once credit has come in.
explanation.definitionFit: To call off a plan or event is to axe it, which is an informal sense of the word.

clue.text: Celebrated retaining Latin in informal speech

indicators.note: retaining says the word for celebrated keeps the abbreviation inside

parts.note: to sing of something is to celebrate it, so sang means celebrated

explanation.surface: Famous scholars kept Latin in everyday chat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Celebrated' looks like an adjective meaning famous, but it is the past tense of a verb: they sang its praises.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual vocabulary outside standard usage is colloquial language.

clue.text: Grammar school shown in trade film

indicators.note: shown in says the school abbreviation appears inside the word for trade

parts.note: to buy is to trade money for goods

explanation.surface: A grammar school is featured in a film about commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1991 Warren Beatty gangster picture about Bugsy Siegel is a film.

clue.text: Nuggets of data on a flyer

indicators.note: on says the bird word comes before the data word in this across answer

parts.note: a tit is a small bird, a flyer
bits are units of computer data

explanation.surface: Snippets of information printed on a leaflet.
explanation.definitionFit: Small tasty morsels, of food or gossip, are little nuggets.

clue.text: Dr Silver claims victory with scores level

indicators.note: claims says the metal symbol takes the triumph word inside it

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A doctor called Silver says he has won when the game ended even.
explanation.definitionFit: A game finishing with the scores level is a tie; the participle describes a side currently tied.

clue.text: Film man signs Lineker by arrangement

indicators.note: by arrangement says the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A film company signs up the footballer Gary Lineker by mutual agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: Gary Lineker is a former England footballer and British TV presenter.
